title: A Shot of Faith (to the Head): Be a Confident Believer in an Age of Cranky Atheists
author: Mitch Stokes
target_audience: Christian readers seeking intellectual and philosophical support for their faith
Believers challenged by contemporary atheistic arguments
College students and young adults navigating secular environments
General readers interested in the intersection of faith and reason
core_themes: Defending the rationality of Christian faith
Responding to arguments from New Atheism
Epistemology and the justification of religious belief
Misconceptions about science, faith, and reason
Encouragement for confident faith in a skeptical world
primary_purpose: To equip Christians with philosophical tools and arguments, fostering a rational and confident faith that can withstand the critiques commonly offered by contemporary atheists, especially in intellectual or secular environments.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, accessible, and sometimes humorous; incorporates philosophical analysis with story-driven examples
structure_format.organization: Arranged in short chapters grouped in sections addressing faith and reason, science and Christianity, and the rationality of faith

key_concepts_lessons: Religious belief, specifically Christian faith, can be both rational and intellectually defensible.
Many popular criticisms of faith—such as the idea that it is irrational or in conflict with science—are based on misunderstandings or oversimplifications.
Philosophical reasoning can provide strong support for belief in God, drawing on work by thinkers such as Alvin Plantinga.
Atheism has its own faith commitments; doubting everything is not a neutral or purely rational stance.
Believers need not be intimidated by atheistic rhetoric or feel forced to abandon rationality.
notable_features: Uses humor and approachable language to explain complex philosophical ideas
Engages directly with popular atheist writers and arguments
Draws heavily from contemporary philosophy of religion
Encourages lay readers to engage intellectually with faith
cultural_historical_context: Published amidst the rise of 'New Atheism' led by public intellectuals such as Richard Dawkins, Sam Harris, and Christopher Hitchens, the book addresses the renewed public debate about the rationality of faith and seeks to reassure believers facing criticism in increasingly secular or skeptical cultural contexts.
reception_impact: Praised by Christian readers and apologists for its clarity, humor, and robust philosophical engagement
Noted as accessible to those without an academic background in philosophy
Sometimes critiqued by skeptics for oversimplifying atheist arguments or sidestepping some objections
Served to boost intellectual confidence among lay Christians
comparable_titles: Reason for God by Timothy Keller
The Language of God by Francis S. Collins
A Manual for Creating Atheists by Peter Boghossian (as a contrasting atheist perspective)
